q.t: Find the mean of 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
q.e: Mean = total ÷ how many = 30 ÷ 5 = 6. It is the value each would have if the total were shared equally.

q.t: Find the median of 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11.
q.e: The median is the middle value once the data is in order. Of 5 values the 3rd is in the middle: 7.

q.t: Find the mode of 2, 3, 3, 5, 7, 3.
q.e: The mode is the value that appears most often. 3 appears three times.

q.t: Find the range of 4, 9, 1 and 7.
q.e: Range = largest − smallest = 9 − 1 = 8. It shows how spread out the data is.

q.t: Find the mean of the first five natural numbers.
Find the median of 4, 1 and 7.
q.e: Put them in order first: 1, 4, 7. The middle one is 4.

q.t: In tally marks, the number 5 is shown as:
o: Four upright strokes with one stroke across them
q.e: Bundling in fives makes counting quick — you can count 5, 10, 15 …

q.t: Data arranged in ascending or descending order is called:
q.e: Raw data is jumbled; arranged data (an array) makes the smallest, largest and middle easy to see.

q.t: The mean of a set of numbers equals:
o: Sum of the numbers ÷ how many numbers
q.e: The mean shares the total equally among all the values.

q.t: The value that occurs most often in a set of data is the:
q.e: Mode = the most ‘fashionable’ value.

q.t: Find the median of 12, 7, 9, 15, 10 and 11.
q.e: In order: 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 15. With an even count there are two middle values, so take their mean: (10 + 11) ÷ 2 = 10.5.

q.t: Find the mean of 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35.
q.e: Total 125 ÷ 5 = 25. (Evenly spaced numbers have the middle one as their mean.)

q.t: The mean of 6 numbers is 12. What is their sum?
q.e: Mean = sum ÷ count, so sum = mean × count = 12 × 6 = 72.

q.t: Find the mode of 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7.
q.e: 6 appears three times, more than any other value.

q.t: Find the mean of the first six even natural numbers.
The mean of 3, 7, x and 10 is 7. Find x.
q.e: The sum must be 4 × 7 = 28. So x = 28 − 20 = 8.

q.t: Find the median of the first seven prime numbers.
q.e: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 — the 4th value is in the middle: 7. (1 is not a prime.)

q.t: In a test, 3 students scored 5 marks, 5 students scored 6 marks and 2 students scored 7 marks. Find the mean mark.
q.e: Total marks = 15 + 30 + 14 = 59 for 10 students: 59 ÷ 10 = 5.9. Each mark must be counted as many times as it occurs.

q.t: Find the range of 23, 45, 12, 38 and 29.
q.e: Largest 45 − smallest 12 = 33.

q.t: Find the mean of 2.5, 3.5, 4.5 and 5.5.
The mean of 5 numbers is 18. One number is removed and the mean of the remaining 4 is 16. Which number was removed?
q.e: Totals: 5 × 18 = 90 before and 4 × 16 = 64 after. The removed number is 90 − 64 = 26.

q.t: The mean of 10 numbers is 15. Each number is increased by 3. Find the new mean.
q.e: Each of the 10 numbers gains 3, so the total gains 30 and the mean gains 30 ÷ 10 = 3.

q.t: The mean of x, x + 2, x + 4, x + 6 and x + 8 is 11. Find x.
q.e: The sum is 5x + 20 = 55, so x = 7. (The mean of evenly spaced numbers is the middle one, x + 4 = 11.)

q.t: The data 5, 8, x, 14, 20, 21 is in ascending order and its median is 12. Find x.
q.e: With 6 values the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (x + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, so x = 10.

q.t: A batsman averages 40 runs over 8 innings. After the 9th innings his average is 42. How many runs did he score in the 9th innings?
q.e: Totals: 9 × 42 = 378 and 8 × 40 = 320. The 9th innings gave 378 − 320 = 58.

q.t: Find the mean of the first 10 natural numbers.
Find the mode of 2, 3, 4, 3, 2, 3, 5, 2, 3.
q.e: Count each: 2 appears 3 times, 3 appears 4 times, 4 and 5 once each. The mode is 3.

q.t: In a class, 20 boys have a mean weight of 45 kg and 30 girls have a mean weight of 40 kg. Find the mean weight of the whole class (in kg).
q.e: Total weight = 900 + 1200 = 2100 kg for 50 students: 42 kg. It is closer to 40 because there are more girls.

q.t: Every value in a data set is multiplied by 2. The mean:
q.e: The total doubles while the number of values stays the same, so the mean doubles.

q.t: Find the median of the first 10 multiples of 3.
q.e: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30. The 5th and 6th are 15 and 18; their mean is 16.5.

q.t: The mean of 25 observations is 36. The mean of the first 13 is 32 and the mean of the last 13 is 39. Find the 13th observation.
q.e: First 13 total 416 and last 13 total 507. Together 923 — but that counts the 13th twice. The real total is 900, so the 13th is 923 − 900 = 23.

q.t: The mean of 10 numbers was worked out as 20. Later it was found that one number, 35, had been misread as 25. Find the correct mean.
q.e: The wrong total was 200. Correct total = 200 − 25 + 35 = 210, so the mean is 21.

q.t: The data 3, 5, 7, x, 11 is in ascending order and its mean equals its median. Find x.
q.e: The median is the middle value, 7. So the mean is 7: (26 + x) ÷ 5 = 7 → x = 9. (It fits between 7 and 11 ✓.)

q.t: The data 4, 6, x, 6, 4, 9 has exactly ONE mode, and that mode is 4. Find x.
q.e: Without x, both 4 and 6 appear twice. For 4 alone to be the mode, x must be another 4.

q.t: The average of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 27. Find the largest of them.
q.e: For evenly spaced numbers the average is the middle one, so they are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31.

q.t: The average age of 30 students is 12 years. When the teacher’s age is included, the average becomes 13 years. How old is the teacher?
q.e: Totals: 31 × 13 = 403 and 30 × 12 = 360. The teacher adds 403 − 360 = 43.

q.t: The mean of p and q is 10, the mean of q and r is 14, and the mean of p and r is 12. Find the mean of p, q and r.
q.e: p + q = 20, q + r = 28, p + r = 24. Adding: 2(p + q + r) = 72, so p + q + r = 36 and the mean is 12.

q.t: The value 10 occurs 3 times, 20 occurs f times and 30 occurs 2 times. The mean is 19. Find f.
A data set has 11 different values. The largest value is increased by 10. The median:
q.e: The median is the 6th value in order. Making the largest even larger does not move the middle. (The mean WOULD change.)

q.t: The mean of 6 numbers is 15. A seventh number is added and the mean becomes 17. Find the seventh number.
q.e: Totals: 7 × 17 = 119 and 6 × 15 = 90. The new number is 119 − 90 = 29.
